OceanofPDF.com CHAPTER 1 We Didn’t Exactly “Build” Artificial Intelligence When I think about DeepMind’s AlphaGo artificial intelligence (AI) engine defeating Lee Sedol at the extremely creative and complex game of Go in 2016, I am reminded of a sea slug. Eric Kandel and the Sea Slug In some breakthrough research in the 1970s, Eric Kandel, along with two others, was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his pioneering work on the biological basis of learning and memory. 1 Eric’s subject? The Aplysia californica — a sea slug . Not exactly the majestic symbol of intelligence one might expect. And yet, this humble marine slug became one of the most important organisms in the history of neuroscience and began unfolding discoveries of how our brain’s neural networks learn that would eventually lead to teaching computers to learn, to the creation of artificial neural networks, and to artificial intelligence. Why a sea slug? For one simple reason: Its neurons are huge—some of the largest in the animal kingdom. And it has so few of these enormous neurons that researchers could isolate, stimulate, and observe individual neurons and their synapses in real time. Kandel’s experiments showed that learning occurs through physical changes at the synapse, the connection point between neurons. 2 When the slug experienced something repeatedly—such as a mild shock to its tail—its neurons changed the slug’s behavior. The synaptic response grew stronger. The more the experience was reinforced, the more durable the memory became. This synaptic plasticity, Kandel showed, was the biological basis of learning. He famously joked that he could “hook the neuron up to a speaker and listen to it fire”—and in fact, that’s exactly what he did. In his lab, you could literally hear the learning process: neurons firing more rapidly as memory formed. Kandel has spoken about how his friends in the early days of his work thought he was crazy to waste his career studying the sea slug. 3 He had so much promise as a scientist, so why waste it there?
